text.tspan: I used to handle this badly. Time saved on
drafting moved into deeper review, which is
the point.
What changed is simpler than it sounds. The
best results still need a human who knows what
good looks like.
Speed is not quality.
Maybe obvious. Still true for me.
AI literacy includes knowing when not to use
it.
I rewrite outputs in my own voice before
anything ships.
Policy beats vibes when tools move this fast.
We ban pasting confidential client data into
public tools. Non-negotiable.
Human judgment is still the product.
Time saved on drafting moved into deeper
review, which is the point.
Train people on evaluation, not only on
prompting tricks.
I use it to generate test cases I might have
missed.
Policy beats vibes when tools move this fast.
We log where AI helped and where it created
rework.
If you cannot explain the output, you cannot
ship the output.
The best results still need a human who knows
what good looks like.
Train people on evaluation, not only on
prompting tricks.
I keep a checklist: source, accuracy, tone,
and permission.
Speed is not quality.
We label AI-assisted drafts so reviewers know
what to scrutinize.
Human judgment is still the product.
Time saved on drafting moved into deeper
review, which is the point.
